title: A pervasive RT–qPCR artifact inflates RNA knockdown by RNA-targeting CRISPR - Nature Biotechnology
gist: Johns Hopkins researchers show that guide RNAs copurify with cellular RNA and inhibit reverse transcription, so RT–qPCR amplicons that span or sit just upstream of a gRNA binding site systematically overstate knockdown by RNA-targeting CRISPR systems (Csm, PspCas13b, CasRx). Catalytically dead enzymes produced up to 90% 'knockdown' that did not exist at the protein level; the fix is a strand-displacing reverse transcriptase such as ultraMarathonRT, or downstream amplicons.

insights.claim: RT–qPCR amplicons that span a CRISPR guide RNA binding site systematically overstate RNA knockdown efficiency because copurified guide RNAs inhibit the reverse transcription step, not because the target transcript was degraded.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Published knockdown efficiencies for RNA-targeting CRISPR platforms are a soft data point; diligence on any RNA-editing or RNA-knockdown asset should demand orthogonal protein-level or downstream-amplicon confirmation.
insights.quote: guide RNAs copurify during RNA extraction and inhibit RT–qPCR for amplicons spanning or upstream of the guide RNA binding site, resulting in overestimation of knockdown efficiency across all CRISPR systems tested

insights.claim: A catalytically inactive (RNase-dead) Csm mutant produced apparent knockdown of BRCA1 of 78% with a spanning amplicon and 42% with an upstream amplicon while the downstream amplicon correctly showed none, quantifying the size of the false signal.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: The artifact is not a rounding error — it can manufacture an apparent 78% efficacy from zero real activity, which is the difference between a go and no-go decision on a candidate.
insights.quote: the downstream amplicon correctly showed no KD, whereas spanning (78%) and upstream (42%) amplicons exhibited apparent KD
insights.locator: Because the original XIST and BRCA1 amplicons

insights.claim: For wild-type Csm targeting XIST, a spanning amplicon reported 90% knockdown while a downstream amplicon reported only 35%, meaning real efficiency can be inflated by roughly 2.5-fold in the same experiment.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Headline potency numbers for nuclear-transcript knockdown platforms may need to be discounted by a factor of two or more when re-underwriting the technology.
insights.quote: the spanning amplicon reported strong KD for both WT and RD Csm (90%), whereas the downstream amplicon showed substantially lower KD for WT (35%) and minimal KD for RD (14%
insights.locator: This effect was stronger for XIST

insights.claim: The inflation is not confined to one enzyme class: PspCas13b and CasRx spanning amplicons also reported significant knockdown for catalytically dead versions that had no effect on mCherry protein levels.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: The problem is platform-agnostic, so it touches every RNA-targeting CRISPR program rather than being a single-company reproducibility issue.
insights.quote: Thus, RT–qPCR with spanning amplicons overestimates KD across all systems tested.
insights.locator: We then tested whether other RNA-targeting CRISPR systems

insights.claim: Residual protein is ruled out as the cause of the artifact because Proteinase K treatment of extracted RNA failed to rescue the spanning amplicon signal, pointing to the nucleic acid rather than the ribonucleoprotein as the inhibitor.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Labs that added protease cleanup as a fix have not solved the problem and their revised numbers are still wrong.
insights.locator: To determine the mechanism underlying RT–qPCR misquantification

insights.claim: Spiking a synthetic mature guide RNA directly into the reverse transcription reaction reproduced concentration-dependent false knockdown for upstream and spanning amplicons, establishing that the guide RNA alone is sufficient to cause the artifact.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A clean, cheap positive control any lab or diligence team can run to test whether a reported knockdown number is real.
insights.quote: Thus, gRNA alone is sufficient to inhibit RT–qPCR.
insights.locator: Next we hypothesized that gRNAs copurify

insights.claim: Inhibition happens during reverse transcription rather than during qPCR, since spiking guide RNA into the qPCR step alone caused much less inhibition and RNase treatment of finished cDNA did not rescue the affected amplicons.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Any mitigation has to change the RT enzyme or chemistry; swapping polymerases or master mixes downstream will not help.
insights.quote: indicating that inhibition occurs primarily during RT

insights.claim: The inhibition is distance-dependent with a fitted decay constant of 170 nucleotides (95% CI 73–390 nt) and disappears beyond roughly 500 nucleotides upstream, giving a concrete design rule for primer placement.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: An actionable, quantitative rule of thumb: place amplicons more than ~500 nt upstream or anywhere downstream of the guide site to avoid the artifact.
insights.quote: decay constant 170 nt, 95% confidence interval, 73–390 nt
insights.locator: Fig. 2 legend, d, Relative expression of all RT–qPCR amplicons

insights.claim: Expressing guide RNA from a plasmid without the Csm proteins produced no apparent knockdown, implying the effector proteins are required to stabilize and accumulate guides to the level at which they contaminate downstream assays.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Artifact severity scales with effector expression, so the most highly engineered, high-activity constructs are the most likely to produce inflated numbers.
insights.quote: suggesting that Csm proteins are required to stabilize gRNAs in cells, enabling accumulation and copurification
insights.locator: Transfection of a gRNA plasmid alone

insights.claim: ultraMarathonRT, a processive reverse transcriptase with strong strand-displacement activity, eliminated the artifact entirely: RNase-dead Csm and RNase-dead PspCas13b produced no apparent knockdown with any amplicon under uMRT.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Creates a specific reagent demand pull for strand-displacing RT enzymes in every CRISPR-RNA lab; uMRT was supplied by RNAConnect, a named commercial source.
insights.quote: With uMRT, RD Csm and RD PspCas13b produced no apparent KD with any amplicon
insights.locator: Although downstream amplicons avoid the artifact

insights.claim: A 3′ dideoxycytidine-capped antisense oligonucleotide complementary to the mature guide rescued spanning and upstream amplicons in a concentration-dependent way, providing a second, cheap mitigation that needs no enzyme swap.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Labs unwilling to change RT chemistry have a low-cost oligo-based workaround, which also serves as a diagnostic that the artifact is present.

insights.claim: The authors' recommended standard is to keep spanning amplicons but pair them with a processive strand-displacing reverse transcriptase, or otherwise use conventional RT with downstream amplicons, always backed by an orthogonal assay.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A likely new methodological convention for the field; journals and reviewers adopting it would reset the comparability of past and future knockdown claims.
insights.quote: We recommend quantifying RNA-targeting CRISPR KD using spanning amplicons with processive, strand-displacing RTs, such as uMRT
insights.locator: We recommend quantifying RNA-targeting CRISPR KD

insights.claim: The same class of artifact may distort knockdown measurements for siRNA, shRNA and antisense oligonucleotides, extending the reproducibility question well past CRISPR into established RNA therapeutic modalities.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: If it holds, preclinical potency data across the RNAi and ASO field is subject to the same discount, which is a broad sector-level diligence flag.
insights.quote: Related artifacts may also influence siRNA, shRNA and ASO KD measurements
insights.locator: In summary, gRNA-target binding can inhibit RT–qPCR

insights.claim: RNA sequencing readouts can also be corrupted whenever cDNA synthesis is performed without prior RNA fragmentation, widening the exposure from targeted qPCR assays to transcriptome-wide datasets.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Long-read and unfragmented RNA-seq protocols used to validate knockdown may need re-running; a hidden cost line for platform companies.
insights.quote: RNA sequencing may also be affected when cDNA synthesis occurs without previous RNA fragmentation.
insights.locator: In summary, gRNA-target binding can inhibit RT–qPCR

insights.claim: Phenol–chloroform (TRIzol-style) extraction, which enriches small RNAs, is expected to make guide RNA carryover and therefore the artifact worse than column-based extraction.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Protocol choice is a hidden variable explaining why some labs see inflated knockdown and others do not — useful when reconciling contradictory datasets.
insights.quote: Phenol–chloroform extraction, which enriches small RNAs, may exacerbate gRNA carryover.
insights.locator: Artifact magnitude probably depends on gRNA abundance

insights.claim: Oligo(dT) priming should inhibit all upstream amplicons because reverse transcription initiates from the poly(A) tail, making a very common priming strategy maximally vulnerable to the artifact.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Datasets generated with oligo(dT) rather than random hexamers deserve the heaviest discount when re-reading published potency.
insights.quote: Oligo(dT) priming may inhibit all upstream amplicons because RT initiates from the poly(A) tail.
insights.locator: Artifact magnitude probably depends on gRNA abundance

insights.claim: The prevailing explanation that catalytically dead effectors cause knockdown by binding within open reading frames and blocking translation or nuclear export is contradicted by apparent knockdown of XIST, a transcript that is neither translated nor exported.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A published biological mechanism is being replaced by a technical artifact — a reminder that mechanistic stories built on RT–qPCR endpoints can be entirely spurious.
insights.quote: However, RD Csm produced apparent KD of XIST (Fig. 1c), which is neither translated nor exported.
insights.locator: Apparent KD by RD Csm has been attributed to

insights.claim: Reported knockdown efficiencies from the original Csm transcript-targeting work were likely inflated because the published XIST and BRCA1 amplicons also spanned the guide binding sites.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Specific prior claims about the Csm system's advantage over Cas13 need re-benchmarking before being used to justify platform selection.
insights.quote: Because the original XIST and BRCA1 amplicons also spanned the gRNA binding sites, reported WT Csm KD efficiencies may have been inflated.
insights.locator: Because the original XIST and BRCA1 amplicons

insights.claim: Flow-cytometry protein measurement of an mCherry reporter, read from the same sample as the RNA, was the decisive orthogonal assay that exposed the artifact — binding alone did not reduce protein while spanning amplicons claimed it did.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A cheap dual-readout reporter design is the practical diligence tool for validating any RNA-knockdown claim before committing capital.
insights.quote: Thus, binding alone does not explain apparent KD by RD Csm.
insights.locator: To test whether binding alone induces RNA decay
